Tulsa area teens can compete for $10,000 in national video contest

Local teens can create short videos about personal finance for a chance to win thousands of dollars in the Lights, Camera, Save! contest.

Brooke Cox
October 1, 2026 09:42 AM
1 min read
  • Copy
    Link copied
  • Email
  • Print
TULSA, Okla. -
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:44
Instaread

First Oklahoma Bank is encouraging Tulsa-area teens to put their creativity and financial knowledge to work in a national video contest offering up to $10,000 in prizes.

The Lights, Camera, Save! video contest challenges teens to create short videos encouraging their peers to develop smart money habits.

Who can enter the contest?

The contest is open to students ages 13 to 18. Entries will be accepted from Oct. 1 through Dec. 1, 2026.

Students must create an original video that is 30 seconds or less and focuses on a personal finance topic.

Topics can include:

  • Saving money
  • Budgeting
  • Paying for college
  • Building credit
  • Protecting against identity theft

Students interested in participating can download an entry form through First Oklahoma Bank.

What can students win?

National winners will receive cash prizes based on their placement:

  • First place: $10,000
  • Second place: $5,000
  • Third place: $2,500

How will the videos be judged?

Videos will be evaluated based on the strength of their financial message, production quality and creativity.

Local winners will advance to the national competition. National finalists will be selected through a combination of judging and public voting.

Why First Oklahoma Bank is encouraging teens to enter

First Oklahoma Bank Senior Vice President and Retail Banking Manager Katy Hedrick said the contest gives students an opportunity to learn about money management while developing communication and digital media skills.

“Financial decisions begin at a young age, and this contest encourages students to think creatively about money management while developing valuable communication and digital media skills,” Hedrick said.

She said the bank is encouraging students throughout its communities to participate and share ideas that could help their peers build strong financial futures.
